While it may be tough to ditch Wissa before he faces Crystal Palace on Sunday, there are no guarantees that he will continue in a number nine role at Selhurst Park, particularly with Will Osula (£5.8m) building his fitness.

The Toffees fell behind shortly after the half-time interval at Hill Dickinson Stadium, before a brace from Thierno Barry and a well-taken strike by Dewsbury-Hall sealed a third consecutive win in the space of eight days.
But Barry proved too hot for Coventry to handle, netting twice in the space of just five minutes to turn the game in Everton 's favour.
Barry has already reached 10 goals this season, surpassing his total for the entire 2025-26 campaign.
Just four minutes after falling behind, the in-form Barry powered an emphatic header beyond Rushworth after meeting Mykolenko’s looping far-post cross.

And five minutes later, Barry turned the contest completely in Everton’s favour with a scrappy goal, bundling the ball over the line from Tyrique George ’s deep delivery before a VAR review confirmed the effort despite Coventry’s handball claims.

The Blues moved into fifth in the Premier League table ahead of this weekend's round of matches, having to come from behind to Yann Gboho's 52nd-minute opener courtesy of a quickfire double from Thierno Barry, before the Frenchman turned provider to see Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall seal the win nine minutes from time.

The Blues came from behind to beat Frank Lampard’s Sky Blues at Hill Dickinson Stadium – with Barry netting Everton’s first and second of the game, before Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall added a third courtesy of the Frenchman's assist.

The Toffees had to recover from Yann Gboho's 52nd-minute opener as Barry headed home Vitalii Mykolenko's cross four minutes later, before taking his goal tally to 10 for the season when he bundled in Tyrique George's centre just past the hour mark.

Three points – which lifted Everton into fifth place in the Premier League table ahead of this weekend's round of matches – were then secured against Frank Lampard's top-flight newcomers nine minutes from time when Barry slid in Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall to blast past Carl Rushworth.

Garner joins Harrison Armstrong and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall in central midfield, flanked by wingers Tyrique George and Dibling, with striker Thierno Barry looking to add to his tally of 10 goal involvements for the season so far.

But after looking back on the non-penalty award which also involved Thierno Barry I could question whether VAR could have easily asked the referee to have another look at the incident, but chose not to.

Goals from William Osula (£5.8m) and Harvey Barnes (£6.1m) secured the points, although the biggest FPL talking point came before kick-off, with Yoane Wissa (£6.1m) and Malick Thiaw (£5.0m) both benched.
Matthias Jaissle made five changes to his starting XI, with Wissa, Thiaw and Sven Botman (£5.0m) among those dropping to the bench.

While it may be tough to ditch Wissa before he faces Crystal Palace on Sunday, there are no guarantees that he will continue in a number nine role at Selhurst Park, particularly with Will Osula (£5.8m) building his fitness.

You get the feeling that things could quickly unravel for Newcastle if they fall behind, too, so there are surely safer bets than Wissa for the upcoming period, like Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6.0m) and Nicolas Jackson (£6.6m).

The Toffees fell behind shortly after the half-time interval at Hill Dickinson Stadium, before a brace from Thierno Barry and a well-taken strike by Dewsbury-Hall sealed a third consecutive win in the space of eight days.
But Barry proved too hot for Coventry to handle, netting twice in the space of just five minutes to turn the game in Everton 's favour.
Barry has already reached 10 goals this season, surpassing his total for the entire 2025-26 campaign.
Just four minutes after falling behind, the in-form Barry powered an emphatic header beyond Rushworth after meeting Mykolenko’s looping far-post cross.

And five minutes later, Barry turned the contest completely in Everton’s favour with a scrappy goal, bundling the ball over the line from Tyrique George ’s deep delivery before a VAR review confirmed the effort despite Coventry’s handball claims.

The Blues moved into fifth in the Premier League table ahead of this weekend's round of matches, having to come from behind to Yann Gboho's 52nd-minute opener courtesy of a quickfire double from Thierno Barry, before the Frenchman turned provider to see Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall seal the win nine minutes from time.

The Blues came from behind to beat Frank Lampard’s Sky Blues at Hill Dickinson Stadium – with Barry netting Everton’s first and second of the game, before Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall added a third courtesy of the Frenchman's assist.

The Toffees had to recover from Yann Gboho's 52nd-minute opener as Barry headed home Vitalii Mykolenko's cross four minutes later, before taking his goal tally to 10 for the season when he bundled in Tyrique George's centre just past the hour mark.

Three points – which lifted Everton into fifth place in the Premier League table ahead of this weekend's round of matches – were then secured against Frank Lampard's top-flight newcomers nine minutes from time when Barry slid in Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall to blast past Carl Rushworth.

Garner joins Harrison Armstrong and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall in central midfield, flanked by wingers Tyrique George and Dibling, with striker Thierno Barry looking to add to his tally of 10 goal involvements for the season so far.

But after looking back on the non-penalty award which also involved Thierno Barry I could question whether VAR could have easily asked the referee to have another look at the incident, but chose not to.

The North Londoners brought Konsa to the Emirates Stadium in the summer transfer market in a well-timed move from Aston Villa in a deal worth £55m.

Ezri Konsa leads Anfield defensive masterclass For the first time in the Premier League era, Liverpool did not register a single shot on target in a game at Anfield, a mark that highlights the outstanding collective defending and the performance of the centre-back pairing.

It's too simplistic to say that Villa lost Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Emiliano Martinez, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins – the transfer fees those players attracted were vital – but the turnover meant that their recruitment had to be all but perfect just for the club to stand still.

In teeming rain at the Emirates Stadium, Arsenal’s centre-backs provided the key moments in front of goal, with Konsa netting for the first time since his arrival from Aston Villa and Gabriel making the points safe midway through the second half.

However, the North London giants belatedly bagged their first corner goal of the campaign to draw first blood against Everton on October 24, as Konsa struck his first Gunners goal at the back stick following an episode of penalty-box pinball.
Konsa opened the scoring inside seven minutes in north London, prodding home from close range after Martin Odegaard's dangerous corner popped up and was clawed on to the crossbar by Jordan Pickford.

It was a period of substantial change for the Villans, who lost Amadou Onana to an ACL injury during the World Cup, Youri Tielemans to Manchester United , Ezri Konsa to Arsenal, Ollie Watkins to Al-Hilal, and Morgan Rogers and Emiliano Martinez to Chelsea .
